newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel cabinet debates size of West Bank pullback.
newsitem.headline: Israel cabinet debates size of West Bank pullback.

text.p: Israel's cabinet was meeting in a marathon session on Friday to set the scope of a pending troop withdrawal in the West Bank, a pullback which could ease tensions with the Palestinians but strain the ruling coalition.

Israel TV said Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, under U.S. pressure to placate the PLO after approving new Jewish homes in Arab East Jerusalem, proposed to hand over another nine percent of West Bank territory.
At least seven of the 18 cabinet members believed such an offer would be too generous, the report said.

Netanyahu, a right-winger elected nine months ago on a promise to get tough in talks with the Palestinians, is bound by an agreement reached in January to relinquish more West Bank land by Friday. The deal left the extent of the pullback open.

The withdrawal will be the first of three from mainly rural areas, an interim process due to be completed by mid-1998. Final borders are to be decided in permanent status talks scheduled to begin this month.

"I hope the cabinet will reach a decision...that will accelerate the peace process and show the desire of the Israeli government to help bring about a good atmosphere that is free from any pressure," Foreign Minister David Levy told reporters.
Three legislators from parties belonging to the coalition threatened publicly to stop supporting the government in parliament if the pending pullback was too deep.
"I don't see myself as part of the coalition which hands over voluntarily parts of the Land of Israel without having been asked to do so," said Moshe Peled of the nationalist Tsomet party.

The government commands 66 seats in the 120-member parliament but dissenting voices inside the coalition have become stronger since Netanyahu's handover in January of most of the West Bank town of Hebron.
Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai said once the cabinet approved the pullback it would take the army at least 48 hours to implement it.

Israel has handed over only about three percent of West Bank land to Palestinian self-rule since its landmark 1993 peace deal with the PLO, but the territory Israel left contains eight major Arab towns. Israel also has given the PLO civil control in some 450 villages.
Palestinians in the West Bank town of Halhoul, near Hebron, prepared for the end of 30 years of military occupation.
Halhul residents decorated their town with Palestinian flags and pictures of Palestinian President Yasser Arafat and painted storefronts.
"We are going to be free. We will not see Israeli soldiers anymore," said Ashraf Ali Milhem, 15.
In East Jerusalem, a Palestinian lawyer said he would meet Israeli police to discuss their official warning to four Palestinian offices to close by Sunday or be shut.
"We agreed on a meeting for Sunday," Jawad Boulos said. "If we fail to come to conclusions, I will prepare a very detailed (court) appeal against the order."
Israel has said the offices were part of the Palestinian self-rule Authority, which under the interim peace deals cannot operate in Jerusalem.
Israel captured East Jerusalem in the 1967 Middle East war and annexed it, a move not recognised internationally, to claim all of the city as its capital.
Palestinians regard East Jerusalem as the capital of a future state. The sides are due to negotiate the city's fate in talks due to run until May 1999.
